title: CI load priming and baseline reconciler for continuous regression detection
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Introduce a CI-side 'priming + reconciler' mechanism that eliminates transient cold-start noise and reconciles short-term workload shifts against long-term baselines so PRs are only gated for real regressions. This ticket implements a lightweight priming run, an adaptive baseline window, and a reconciler that applies a statistical correction before comparing PR results to the baseline. The goal is to reduce false positives from microburst variance and kernel warm-up while still catching true throughput or p95 regressions in tokens/sec-sensitive workloads.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs execute a <2 minute priming phase for each model configuration that warms caches and populates KV cache profiles
PR gate comparisons use a reconciled baseline that blends long-term median and recent trend (configurable weights) rather than a single snapshot
False-positive rate on historical PRs reduced by >= 60% compared to current gating heuristic (measured on 90-day sample)
Regression detection still maintains >= 90% recall for injected regressions of >= 5% p95 or tokens/sec drop in synthetic workloads
Gating decision metadata (baseline snapshot id, priming trace id, reconciliation parameters, statistical test result) is recorded and surfaced in PR CI artifacts
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Priming: short, deterministic microbench workload to warm JIT/alloc paths and fill KV caches; keep deterministic seed and small corpus to execute within CI budget. 2) Baseline: maintain two windows — long-term (30d median) and short-term (3-7d rolling median). Reconciler computes weighted median and measures drift; if short-term deviates beyond configurable drift threshold, increase weight on short-term to detect real workload shifts. 3) Statistical test: use a non-parametric bootstrap on p95/tokens/sec distributions rather than assuming gaussianity. 4) Decision plumbing: produce a single gating verdict with tie-breaker rules (e.g., require both p95 and tokens/sec to exceed thresholds unless high severity). 5) Observability: publish time-series, effect size, and bootstrap confidence intervals to the PR artifact and runtime dashboard.
implementation_plan: Add a CI priming job in the PR workflow that runs a 90–120s microbench per model variant and stores priming trace artifacts
Extend the baseline store to hold rolling windows and computed medians with snapshot ids; implement APIs to fetch baseline slices
Implement reconciling logic in the gating service: weighted median blend, drift detector, and bootstrap test to compute p-values and effect sizes
Wire gating verdict output to PR status with rich metadata: baseline_snapshot, priming_trace, p-value, effect_size, confidence_interval
Add feature flags to progressively enable reconciler per repo/team and run in shadow mode before blocking PRs
test_plan: Unit tests for reconciler math (weighted medians, drift thresholds, bootstrap CI)
Synthetic regression injection tests: add deterministic regressions (5%, 10%, 20%) to token throughput and p95 and verify detection/recall
Replay historical CI PRs with priming enabled to measure false positive reduction and compare gating outcomes
End-to-end smoke: run CI workflow on staging with reconciler in shadow mode and confirm artifacts are generated and dashboards receive metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow): enable reconciler for 20% of PRs for two weeks; monitor FP/FN, runbooks, and performance overhead
Phase 2 (opt-in): allow repositories to opt into enforced gating with reconciler for another two weeks
Phase 3 (enforce): default reconciler gating for all PRs; keep ability to revert via feature flag
Post-rollout: run a 30-day audit of gating decisions and tune drift thresholds and priming duration
observability: Expose priming run duration, token/sec time series, p95 distribution, bootstrap CI bounds to the Console under project/continuous-perf-gating
Add logs linking PR id -> baseline snapshot id -> priming trace id to simplify triage
Alerting: if shadow-mode FP rate rises >10% or staging fails to detect injected regressions, open an incident and auto-disable reconciler
mitigations: If priming increases CI time too much, fall back to a lighter 'quick-priming' profile limited to 30s for low-priority repos
If reconciling suppresses real regressions under rare workload shifts, require a second-level test (longer synthetic run) before allowing merge
Provide an override label (ci/perf-override) to bypass gating during urgent fixes
